sources.note: Nothing. Section 0.2 Phonology (vol. p. 18 = p. 30) lists consonants, vowels, nasalized vowels and 'tones high (written with acute accent), mid (written with macron), and low (unmarked)' and notes 'extensive tone sandhi'; no word about stress or accent placement. sources.citation: Penner, Kevin L. 2019. Prosodic structure in Ixtayutla Mixtec: Evidence for the foot. PhD dissertation, University of Alberta. 404 pp. DOI 10.7939/r3-10cf-7t94.
sources.note: About Ixtayutla Mixtec (ISO vmj, neighbouring coastal variety), not Jamiltepec: 'the couplet is the locus of stress assignment.. stress is obligatorily realized in a left-headed, bimoraic structure' (Abstract, p. ii-iii). It cites Johnson 1988 only for the three-tone analysis of Jamiltepec (p. 93) and for Jamiltepec word forms (pp. 80, 261); it makes no claim about Jamiltepec stress.

sources.citation: Stark, Sharon & Audrey Johnson. 1986. Diccionario mixteco de San Juan Colorado. Serie de Vocabularios y Diccionarios Indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 29. México: ILV. [San Juan Colorado Mixtec, ISO mjc - a 'closely related dialect' per Johnson 1988:17; NOT in the target's works list, already held by the project;https://archive.org/details/mixtecosanjuancoloradodiccionario]
sources.note: Describes San Juan Colorado Mixtec (mjc), which Johnson 1988:17 lists among the dialects 'closely related to that of Jamiltepec' but which has its own ISO code and Glottolog entry; co-authored by the same Audrey Johnson. It is the nearest explicit stress statement to Jamiltepec but cannot be filed as a jami1235 record.

sources.citation: Pensinger, Brenda J. 1974. Diccionario mixteco-español, español-mixteco: mixteco del este de Jamiltepec, pueblo de Chayuco. Serie de Vocabularios y Diccionarios Indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 18. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano / SEP. 173 pp. (grammar notes pp. 137-146)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'La ortografía mixteca' (pp. 137-138) covers letters and 'Los tonos': 'El mixteco es un idioma tonal.. Hay tres niveles de tono en el mixteco de Chayuco' (alto, medio, bajo). The word 'acento' does not occur in the grammar notes. NB this dictionary describes Chayuco Mixtec ('mixteco del este de Jamiltepec, pueblo de Chayuco', ISO mih, Glottolog chay1249), not Jamiltepec proper; the earlier scan note that called it the Jamiltepec dictionary is confirmed as 'tone described, no stress statement' but for the Chayuco variety.
Nothing; references are only Ethnologue entries for mxt and mih.

sources.citation: Stark Campbell, Sara, Andrea Johnson Peterson & Filiberto Lorenzo Cruz (comps.). 1986. Diccionario mixteco de San Juan Colorado. Serie de Vocabularios y Diccionarios Indígenas 'Mariano Silva y Aceves' 29. México: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the 'Gramática mixteca' §0.2 describes three tones (alto, medio, bajo) and their nine/seven combinations on disyllabic words; 'acento' is used only for the written accent marks. San Juan Colorado Mixtec (ISO mjc) is a separate ISO language, but Johnson 1988:17 lists San Juan Colorado among towns speaking 'dialects closely related to that of Jamiltepec'.

sources.note: The only other work Glottolog and Auderset et al. 2023 name for Santiago Jamiltepec; compares 16 modern Mixtec phonological systems and discusses the bimoraic couplet (p. 460 per Penner 2019), so it is the most likely place for a comparative remark on stress/prominence that covers the coastal (Jamiltepec) area.
